newsitem.title: FRANCE: Debt deal reached for Channel Tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Debt deal reached for Channel Tunnel.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc reached an outline agreement with six bank lenders Tuesday to restructure debt and unpaid interest totalling some 70 billion French francs ($14 billion), a source familiar with the marathon negotiations said.
"There has been a global agreement, the details are being finalised this evening," the source said.
A Eurotunnel spokeswoman declined to comment. In London, National Westminster Bank Plc said talks were continuing but it was optimistic.

Eurotunnel's co-chairmen, Alistair Morton and Patrick Ponsolle, have been in intense negotiations with bankers to break a deadlock over the pricing of a debt-for-equity swap and issuing convertible bonds needed to lighten its debt service.
The president of the Paris commercial court, Jean-Pierre Mattei, was expected to make a statement either Tuesday night or Wednesday on the debt talks, which have been stalled for a year.

Eurotunnel, which operates the rail tunnel opened in May 1994, froze interest payments on its junior-ranked debt in September 1995, unable to bear the debt burden incurred due to cost overruns incurred digging the Franco-British link.
